Saturday Summary: Cosmic Crusader sets sights on Memsie after PB Lawrence victory

The 3-year-olds were out in force on Saturday as spring fever swept over Caulfield, where Hard Kick bounced back to his best in the G3 Vain Stakes, and Rosehill, where Chilly Girl surged home to win the Listed Rosebud. Over in Ruakaka, She's No Saint became Prague's second stakes winner when taking out the G3 Northland Breeders' Stakes.

A strong Saturday of racing signals that early spring is in the air, with quality 3-year-olds taking centre stage across the country, as well as proven Weight-for-age campaigners that take aim at the G2 P.B Lawrence Stakes at Caulfield.

Three-time Group 1 winner Sir Delius again looked in excellent order winning one of the Group trials alongside Warwoven and Enriched on the Kensington, while a couple of 3-year-old winners also caught the eye in an action-packed morning of trials at Randwick.

In 2025/26, Godolphin changed their training model to distribute their horses across several stables and the experiment was a resounding success with 11 Group 1 races won. For this season, the promise of Anamoe’s first crop and with many of their stars remaining in work, they are striving towards a similar lofty goal.
In this instalment of Stable Tours, TTR catches up with Michael Freedman to preview a powerful spring team, headlined by exciting stars such as Ninja, Marhoona, Apocalyptic and Incognito.

The Thoroughbred Report touched base with industry professionals to see who caught their eye at Thursday’s Victorian stallion parades. Vinrock, Observer, Espionage, Growing Empire and Gold Trip were among those who got several mentions.

Breeding horses is about realising a dream, and that dream for HP Thoroughbreds is to produce another champion. Kristen Evans talks to TTR for today's Matings Mix about some of the star mothers in her paddocks and who they will patronise this year.

Savagram headed a strong Wednesday for quality-bred runners, with Wanda’s Spark, I Am Aria and Esha also successful across Australia. These runners all stamped their credentials as exciting spring prospects.
